scope: Read-only boot-disk recovery assessment for primary Chrome-profile testing

policy.constraints: No deletion or movement; no broad apply; preserve user files, worktrees, browser profiles, and caches belonging to active contributors.

groomer_dry_run.result: 17 registered trees: 9 primary, 8 temporary copies; 0 linked worktrees; 0 stale linked worktrees; 3 primary .next caches skipped; 0 bytes reclaimed. Docker engine unavailable, so Docker pruning was skipped.
groomer_dry_run.temporary_tree_ages: 1.6 to 7.0 hours, below the 24-hour stale threshold; dry run marked all KEEP young.

candidate_scan.method: Read-only du, directory age/owner metadata, process listing, and lsof path-reference inspection under /private/tmp.
candidate_scan.result: No eligible campaign-owned disposable artifact large enough to recover the approximately 3 GiB needed to reach 22 GiB was identified. The groomer's listed temporary trees measured at most about 1 GiB each and together are not a material recovery source; no lsof references were found for the inspected named temporary build trees, but their age and uncertain campaign ownership disqualify removal. Other temporary paths are system/app/browser temporary data or unverified owner artifacts and were not considered safe. Active Google Chrome processes and Chrome extension renderers were present, so Chrome profiles and related caches were excluded.

safe_options.action: No cleanup approved by this assessment.
safe_options.basis: No identified artifact met both sufficient size and verified stale/rebuildable ownership criteria.

safe_options.action: Have the adjudicating owner identify a specific artifact or approve a system-managed cleanup target after establishing ownership and lack of active references.
safe_options.basis: The permitted candidates inspected here cannot safely reach the requested free-space target.

result: Insufficient safe cleanup identified to reach either the >20 GiB floor or the preferred 22 GiB target. No files were deleted or moved.
